chapter: Arriving in New York and founding the Afro-Cubans
title: How the band became Machito and his Afro-Cubans
summary: Machito says the name was chosen by the club owner, not by him or Mario, replacing the Cuban New Yorkers name.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: I see. Okay, I got, I got the jist of that. Okay, give the name, as far as you can remember, of the original Machito band. First of all, why did they call it Machito and the Afro-Cubans?

Well, you know, when I was born they called me Macho, not Machito, but this Cuban fellow, he say "Macho, it sound too harsh, too rude. Why don't we call Machito and y su Afro-Cubanos." When I get down there I say no, no, no. Please you go and talk to Iznaga and the rest of the
musicians, because this is a cooperative, I don't want that they think that I want to change the Siboney name, so we wasn't - there was no way out.
Oh, I see. In other words, when you got the job at the—
That was the old Cuban New Yorkers.
Ah Hah, and then you changed it to Machito and the Afro-Cubans?
Bob Smith and another Cuban fellow, so it wasn't my idea. Machito and Afro-Cubans come by accident. That was created by somebody.
Okay. So that, because I always thought that it was Mario who gave that name.
It was way before, so in other words while you were appearing at The Great White Way, you were known as Machito and the Afro-Cubans.
